content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus is the young shoot of the plant Asparagus officinalis. Frozen asparagus cooked with oil is a ready‑to‑eat product that retains most nutrients and its characteristic tender flavor. It is convenient for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the earliest cultivated vegetables, grown for over 2,000 years.
In the United States it is often called the “queen of spring” because of its seasonal appearance.
Freezing preserves up to 90 % of B‑vitamins and vitamin C when the product is flash‑frozen after harvest.
Cooking in oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
Asparagus contains aromatic compounds that give it its distinctive scent.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A serving provides about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Asparagus provides glutathione, vitamin C and vitamin E, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber in asparagus promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The ready‑made product may contain added salt; people with hypertension should check sodium levels.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible persons.

items.title: Added oil
items.content: Since the product is already cooked in oil, total fat intake should be considered.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen asparagus in a skillet, microwave, or steamer. Serve as a side dish, add to salads, pasta, omelets, or incorporate into vegetable mixes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C in the original packaging. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.
